title: Measuring the Two-dimensional Thermal Structures of Protoplanetary Disks
question: How can the 2-D thermal structure T(r,z) of a protoplanetary disk be measured annulus by annulus from optically thick CO isotopologue emission, tested on synthetic models and applied to HD 163296?

evidence.quote: We selected ALMA observations of the HD 163296 disk from the MAPS project (cite: Oberg21).

what.value: HD 163296 geometric parameters from CO J=2-1

evidence.quote: We adopted the geometric parameters measured from the same CO $J$=2$-$1 observations in (cite: Izquierdo23)

what.value: Law et al. best-fit temperature models for comparison

evidence.quote: They deviate from the (cite: Law21) best-fit model profiles, indicating that a single power law is not a good match to the temperature profile.

recipe.method: RADMC-3D LTE raytracing of parametric disk, convolved with 0.1'' beam, noise 2 mJy/beam per channel
assumptions: X_CO=5e-5, T_frz=20 K, sigma_crit=0.01 g cm-2, D_CO=1e-3, CO/13CO=69, CO/C18O=557

recipe.method: disksurf isovelocity-loop peak extraction in three passes, then binning into annuli of half beam FWHM
Moment-8 map (RMS subtracted) via bettermoments, azimuthally averaged along surface with gofish, converted with Planck function
assumptions: Optically thick LTE gas so T_gas = T_b

recipe.method: Forward model T_m with Gaussian or top-hat emitting-region kernel K based on Keplerian width of the emitting region; fit to measured intensity
key_parameters: 16 walkers, 300 steps, 50 burn-in; uniform prior T_m 0-10,000 K
assumptions: Keplerian velocity, thermal broadening, small temperature gradient across emitting region

recipe.method: Fit Keplerian v_peak(r) to extracted velocity profile excluding inner ~5 beams, over 200 surface draws
key_parameters: uniform prior M* 0-5 Msun, 32 walkers, 1000 steps, 300 burn-in

recipe.goal: Infer vertical T(z) in each annulus
recipe.method: Fit T_mid, gamma, a_z per annulus to (z, T_b) of all lines, repeated over N surface realizations
key_parameters: uniform priors T_mid U(0,1500 K), gamma U(0,100), a_z U(0,1); 32 walkers, 50,000 steps, 10,000 burn-in (synthetic tests)
assumptions: Parametric form: isothermal midplane then exponential rise; lines optically thick where T_b>20 K

recipe.method: Same pipeline on MAPS cubes, geometry from Izquierdo23, M* fit from 12CO J=2-1, annuli fitted to r=3.0'' where at least two lines available

evidence.quote: biasing them low by up to $\Delta z/r \approx0.1$ for CO and $\Delta z/r \approx0.15$ for C$^{18}$O
The bias can extend up to 8 times the size of the beam, and the intensity can be underestimated by as much as 50%.

not_stated_but_needed: Which MAPS data products (image cubes, resolution, robust weighting) were used for HD 163296
Prior ranges for the HD 163296 fits if different from synthetic tests
Noise (RMS) values for the MAPS cubes
Number of surface realizations N and radial annulus widths for HD 163296
Which lines were treated as optically thick beyond the T_b<20 K criterion
missing_for_reproduction: Analysis code for the correction and inference not stated as released
Exact MAPS cube versions and beams
score_reason: Method well specified with sampler settings and synthetic model parameters, but code release and exact HD 163296 inputs are not stated.
rediscovery_reason: Public MAPS data and detailed recipe; numeric results such as M*=1.93 Msun can be checked, though some inputs are inherited.
